text:
A: Hello, love, can you hear me? Sorry, I always say that. I'm Joanne, I'm in Gosport.
B: Yes, I can hear you fine. Gemma, Hornchurch. You've got it working, then.
A: Just about! My sister set it up on the phone for me. Erm, what do you do, Gemma? I had you down as a teacher from your picture.
B: Close. Speech and language therapist. Mostly children, self-employed. I did ten years in the NHS first.
A: Oh, that's clever. I'm only in a school kitchen. A primary. Eleven years now.
B: Don't say "only". My mum did school dinners for years in Dagenham. She used to come home with her hands red raw from the big sinks. It's proper hard work.
A: Oh, did she? Ah, bless her. It is, it's the standing that does me. And the lifting the trays. My knees and my back aren't what they was, and I've had a couple of days off lately, and I feel terrible, 'cause the cook's relying on me.
B: Have you said anything to the school? About maybe doing less of the heavy stuff?
A: Erm, no. I worry they'd think I can't do the job, and then, you know. I can't really afford to drop my hours.
B: Sorry, can I be a bit blunt? You've been there eleven years. You know every child's allergies, I'd put money on it. They're not going to want to lose you. If you go in and say "I want to keep doing this, can we adjust the lifting", that's not weakness, that's you planning. Schools have to make reasonable adjustments anyway. Write down what you'd want before you go in, so you don't get flustered.
A: Oh. I hadn't thought of it like that. I would get flustered, you're right.
B: Everyone does. I reread my emails about five times before I send them.
A: Do you? I'd never have guessed, you look ever so organised.
B: I've heard that a lot today.
A: Ha! Sorry. Erm, have you got children yourself?
B: Two. Ruby's eleven, Alfie's eight. You?
A: No, I never did. Just my cat, Biscuit. But I crochet little hats and blankets for the baby unit at QA, the hospital in Portsmouth. The tiny ones, for the prem babies. They're no bigger than a satsuma, some of them.
B: Oh, that's lovely. Alfie was... he had a bit of a rough start. They have those knitted things on the ward. I remember thinking someone's sat and made that.
A: Oh, love. I hope he's alright now?
B: He's fine. He's eight and he wants a dog, so he's very much fine.
A: Ha! Well, tell him a cat's less work. Biscuit just sleeps on my jigsaw.
B: What are you doing at the moment?
A: Thousand-piece, a harbour scene. It's a nightmare, love, it's all sky. Do you do anything like that?
B: Book group. And parkrun. And redoing rooms, which Dean hates.
A: Oh, I'd love to be that busy. I don't know if I've been very interesting, sorry.
B: You have, actually. And book that chat with the school, yeah?
A: I will. Thank you, Gemma. Thank you.
